overview.summary:
This plan keeps the PRD intentionally thin: one story for BUG-002 and one story for BUG-003. Both stories stay in a single execution wave because the requested fixes are independent and small, but the plan constrains ownership so they can still land without merge conflicts.

S01 owns the edit-dialog due-date persistence path and its regression proof. S02 owns the quick-add default-priority path and its regression proof. Any implementation that needs to cross those ownership lines should stop and re-plan rather than widening the story silently.

sharedDecisions.title: Isolate the bug fixes by ownership boundary
sharedDecisions.description: S01 owns edit-dialog due-date persistence behavior and its regression coverage; S02 owns quick-add default-priority behavior and its regression coverage so the two stories can merge cleanly.

sharedDecisions.title: Honor the existing HTML date contract end-to-end
sharedDecisions.description: S01 must preserve the date-only format already emitted by the edit dialog so saved values round-trip back into the same control without widening the scope into broader date-time behavior.

sharedDecisions.title: Make default priority true at creation time
sharedDecisions.description: S02 must ensure quick-add todos are stored and rendered with low priority from the moment they are created, avoiding UI-only fixes that leave persisted state inconsistent.

bindingConstraints.verbatim: Fix BUG-002 and BUG-003 from docs/PRODUCT-BACKLOG.md (Known Defects section) as two independent, thin stories.
Keep each story isolated to its own files; they must merge without conflict.

stories.name: Persist edit-dialog due dates
stories.scope: Todo edits persist a date chosen in the existing edit dialog, and reopening the same todo shows that saved date back in the due-date control. This story includes round-tripping valid date-only input and preserving the existing clear-date behavior. It excludes overdue styling changes, quick-add priority behavior, and any broader date-time redesign.
stories.notes: Own only the edit/update due-date path and its regression proof so the story stays isolated from quick-add priority work.

stories.name: Default quick-add priority to low
stories.scope: Todos created from the quick-add form start with the documented low priority so the created record and rendered todo row both show a valid priority immediately. This story includes defaulting creation-time state for quick-add flows and proving the visible result through regression coverage. It excludes edit-dialog due-date persistence, priority redesign, and changes to other todo creation flows beyond what is required to make quick-add correct.
stories.notes: Own only the quick-add default-priority path and its regression proof so the story remains merge-safe beside S01.

executionNotes: Execute S01 and S02 in parallel within W1. Preserve the PRD isolation rule by keeping S01 on the edit-dialog due-date persistence surface and S02 on the quick-add default-priority surface; if either fix requires crossing into the other's ownership boundary, stop and regenerate the plan instead of broadening the write set.
